ds: Offenders build online trust over weeks or months, then steer the victim into sending money for an emergency or into a fake investment platform that shows fabricated gains. Funds typically flow through exchanges, mule accounts and offshore networks.

src.t: FinCEN, Alert on prevalent virtual currency investment scam commonly known as pig butchering (2023)

cn.rt: Victims send repeated payments to fake partners or platforms, sometimes funded by personal loans; branch staff may spot coercion.

rat: Victim payments to exchanges and offshore accounts.

ind.n: Escalating transfers to crypto exchanges by a first-time buyer
ind.cx: Victim-side: a customer with no crypto history makes repeated, rising purchases and onward transfers to external wallets within weeks.
ind.ds: Victim-side: a customer with no crypto history makes repeated, rising purchases and onward transfers to external wallets within weeks.

ind.n: Customer mentions an online partner never met
ind.cx: Victim-side: explanations of payment mention a recent online relationship, overseas partner, military or offshore worker who cannot meet.
ind.ds: explanations of payment mention a recent online relationship, overseas partner, military or offshore worker who cannot meet.

ind.n: Investment platform with unlicensed or cloned identity
ind.cx: Victim-side: payments go to a platform that lacks regulatory authorisation, imitates a legitimate firm or is hosted on a recently registered domain.
ind.ds: Payments go to operators, platforms or merchants that are absent from regulatory registers, imitate a legitimate firm, or process under a disguised merchant category.
ind.cn: Unlicensed or cloned operator receiving payments

ind.n: Funds routed to multiple small accounts then consolidated
ind.cx: Mule-side: scam proceeds are split across many personal and corporate accounts before consolidation and cash-out.
ind.fp: Payroll or marketplace payouts with similar structure.
ind.ds: Mule-side: scam proceeds are split across many personal and corporate accounts before consolidation and cash-out.

ind.n: Large 'withdrawal fee' or 'tax' payment to release gains
ind.cx: Victim-side: after a seemingly profitable period, the customer sends further funds to unlock profits.
ind.fp: Genuine exit fees at regulated platforms.
ind.ds: Payments are made as fees or taxes supposedly needed to release a prize, loan, inheritance or gains.
ind.cn: Fee or tax payment demanded to release funds

ind.n: Loan, credit card or remortgage taken to fund transfers
ind.cx: Victim-side: the customer draws credit or equity shortly before sending money away, often citing a vague purpose.
ind.ds: Victim-side: the customer draws credit or equity shortly before sending money away, often citing a vague purpose.

ind.n: Gift-card or peer-to-peer payments to a single remote contact
ind.cx: Victim-side: regular payments or vouchers sent to one beneficiary overseas with emotional narratives.
ind.ds: Victim-side: regular payments or vouchers sent to one beneficiary overseas with emotional narratives.

ind.n: Accounts used as pass-through for overseas scam operations
ind.cx: Mule-side: recruited accounts receive victim funds and convert quickly to stablecoins or wire abroad.
ind.ds: recruited accounts receive victim funds and convert quickly to stablecoins or wire abroad.

ind.n: Customer is isolated and defensive about intervention
ind.cx: Victim-side: customer insists on completing payments, becomes upset with questions or states friends and family do not understand.
ind.ds: customer insists on completing payments, becomes upset with questions or states friends and family do not understand.

ctl.ds: Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

ctl.n: Dynamic payment friction and scam warnings
ctl.ds: Risk-scored payments trigger a purpose question and a tailored scam warning, or a call-back, before release to the customer. It gives the customer a chance to reconsider and interrupts payments made under deception.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

Allows customers to nominate a trusted contact and applies tailored handling and permitted escalation when vulnerability is flagged. It adds a safeguard for customers more exposed to manipulation or coercion.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.
Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
Clusters customers, vendors and entities that share addresses, phones, devices, officers or bank details, including against staff records. It reveals common control and hidden relationships.

Provides targeted messaging that helps customers recognise scam scripts and mule recruitment, verify requests independently and use trusted routes for giving or paying. It reduces victimisation and unwitting participation.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.
